title: Hierarchical cellulose-based tungsten trioxide–silicon dioxide hybrid for synergistic adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of organic contaminants
content: The contamination of natural water sources by hazardous substances such as toxic dyes and mycotoxins has emerged as a serious health and environmental issue due to their high toxicity and resistance to conventional treatment methods. In this work, a novel, sustainable photocatalytic-adsorptive material derived from naturally occurring sources, based on cellulose, SiO2, and WO3, was successfully synthesized and applied to remove water pollutants such as ochratoxin A, rhodamine B, and malachite green. SiO2 nanoparticles were prepared to provide a high surface area for the adsorption of organic pollutants, whereas WO3 nanoparticles act as a visible-light-responsive photocatalyst for the degradation of organic pollutants. The incorporation of cellulose, a biopolymer extracted from rice husks, significantly increases the adsorption of mycotoxins and toxic organic dyes. The resulting WO3@SiO2@cellulose hybrid exhibited dual functionality, enabling efficient adsorption followed by photocatalytic degradation under natural sunlight. The WO3@SiO2@cellulose hybrid degraded MG and RB by up to 98% and 99.3%, respectively. The high removal efficiency is attributed to a synergistic effect involving pollutant–surface interactions, increased surface area, and strong charge separation. The results demonstrate that WO3@SiO2@cellulose hybrid materials offer a promising, eco-friendly platform for the simultaneous adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of ochratoxin A, rhodamine B, and malachite green from contaminated water.
